# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — Host DESKTOP-B8TQK49

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (2024-11-26 04:49:38–05:43:58 UTC), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert log)

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC address | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (confirmed via NBNS name registration and NTLMSSP auth hostname field) |
| AD domain | NEMOTOADS.HEALTH (workgroup alias seen in traffic as NEMOTODES; domain controller NEMOTODES-DC / 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` field, realm NEMOTOADS.HEALTH) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client repurposed as a trojan by an attacker-controlled server. **Signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral:

- HTTP User-Agent literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every C2 request.
- C2 request/response bodies use the NetSupport protocol verbs in plaintext: `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>`.
- Suricata fired exact-match rules: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Client performed a NetSupport-specific geolocation lookup (`GET /location/loca.asp`) to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, standard behavior of the genuine NetSupport client component this trojan is built on.

Infection vector observed in traffic: at 04:50:14 UTC the host resolved and connected via TLS to the typosquat/scam domain `modandcrackedapk.com` (cracked-APK lure, flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI/DNS Lookup`), immediately followed by connections to `classicgrand.com` and `confirmsubscription.com` — consistent with a fake-CAPTCHA/"ClickFix" redirect chain. The RAT C2 session began 31 seconds later (04:50:45 UTC) directly to a hardcoded IP with no preceding DNS lookup, indicating the C2 address is embedded in the dropped configuration rather than resolved dynamically.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2, HTTP-over-443 beaconing (`POST /fakeurl.htm`), 58 check-ins observed from 04:50:45 to 05:43:29 UTC at roughly 60-second intervals.

**Malicious / suspicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolved to 193.42.38.139 (ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP-flagged lure domain, initial access chain)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 13.56.30.207, 52.8.34.0
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 / 104.26.0.231 / 172.67.68.212 (legitimate NetSupport infrastructure used by the RAT for IP geolocation)

**Malicious URLs**
- `https://modandcrackedapk.com/` (TLS SNI, 04:50:40 UTC)
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 polling endpoint, 58 requests)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (geolocation lookup, returned coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877`)

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No executable payload was captured in the clear. The drop/stage occurred over TLS to `193.42.38.139:443` (encrypted, content not recoverable from this capture) or via a clipboard/ClickFix-style execution path that never produced an HTTP file transfer. No file objects other than `.htm`/`.asp`/`.txt` text artifacts were extractable via HTTP object export, and none of those correspond to a payload binary — **no SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence.**

**Supporting Suricata alerts (secondary/noise, not independently actioned)**
- `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt` and related SMBv1/EFSR alerts between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller (10.11.26.3) at 04:50:10–04:50:14 UTC — standard Windows AD/SMB negotiation traffic misfiring on legacy signatures; no evidence in the pcap of successful exploitation or lateral movement tied to this activity.

## Summary

DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user `oboomwald` on NEMOTOADS.HEALTH, was compromised via a cracked-software lure at `modandcrackedapk.com` around 04:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. Within a minute, the host began beaconing to a NetSupport RAT C2 server at `194.180.191.64:443`, confirmed by protocol strings, User-Agent, and multiple ET/ETPRO signature hits, and continued checking in roughly every 60 seconds for the remainder of the capture (through 05:43:29 UTC).
